blurb: Jeju's winter mandarin, grown outdoors. Extra-early (geukjosaeng) fruit ships from mid Oct and early (josaeng) fruit from mid Nov, so the crop runs into February. December is when it is best picked.
Mandarins grown under heat, so they reach shops from late April, long before the open-field crop. Growers run four different heating schedules, which is why supply stretches to late October.
A late-ripening hybrid citrus (mangamryu), one of the larger mandarins that follow plain gyul. Korea's farm agency (the Rural Development Administration) puts it in Nov-Dec.

A late-ripening citrus grown on Jeju. The farm agency gives Jan-Mar, but food merchandiser Kim Jin-yeong argues growers now pick it much earlier for price, so the true season has slid from Feb to late Nov.
caveat: Two answers to one question. The agency's months are Jan-Mar, and Kim says picking has moved earlier.

blurb: A late-ripening citrus that the farm agency lists for Jan-Feb. Feb 2024 shipments were 12,088 t, behind cheonhyehyang at 17,168 t and hallabong at 14,660 t.
A late-ripening citrus that the farm agency lists for Feb-Mar. It was the biggest of the three big late citrus in Feb 2024, with 17,168 t shipped.
A newer citrus bred by Korea's farm agency, which has it ripening in early December.
A newer citrus bred by Korea's farm agency. It starts in Nov or Dec and runs to January.
caveat: The agency gives the start as Nov or Dec, not one month.

blurb: A newer citrus bred by Korea's farm agency, which puts it in late February.
The last of the farm agency's newer citrus, ripening from late March into April. Karahyang follows it as the last citrus of the year.
A Japanese cross introduced in 2008, and the last citrus picked in Korea each year. It is sold as a premium gift. In 2025 the average price was 13,540 won per 3 kg.

Green, unripe mandarins. It is the only fruit with a legal season, Aug 1-Sep 15 under Jeju's rules. In 2026 the count was 233 households and 1,174 t. People use it for cheong syrup, juice, sauces and peel tea.
caveat: Shops often sell this fruit as cheonggyul, a different native citrus picked Mar-Apr.

blurb: A native green citrus picked Mar-Apr in low volume, mainly for medicinal use. It is a different fruit from putgyul, though sellers blur the two.
A citrus made into syrup and tea. Harvest centres on Goheung, which holds a festival each November. People buy boxes at the harvest to make cheong syrup at home.
A summer citrus. Its months come second-hand from a government fruit database, so treat the dates as a lead.
caveat: Hagyul and lemon are listed together as May-Jun and Oct-Jan. Pairing hagyul with May-Jun follows the order of the list, not a stated link.

blurb: Lemon's Oct-Jan window is read second-hand from a government fruit database. No harvest source was found.
caveat: Hagyul and lemon are listed together as May-Jun and Oct-Jan. Pairing lemon with Oct-Jan follows the order of the list, not a stated link.

blurb: A mandarin hybrid that appears only in a list of late-ripening citrus (mangamryu). The pages checked give no season, so it stays off the calendar.
A small citrus eaten whole with the skin on, after a good wash. The pages checked give no season, so it stays off the calendar.
eat: Whole with the skin, after washing

blurb: Over 90% of Korean strawberries are greenhouse crops harvested Nov-Apr. The first flush tastes best, and volume peaks in the third flower cluster, late Feb to early Mar. The open-field season used to be May-Jun.
caveat: Heat delayed November crops in 2024 and 2025.

blurb: Sold from late March, greenhouse fruit first and open-field fruit later. Peak quality is early to mid June, and then the fruit disappears fast. At Garak market, special-grade fruit fell from 55,519 won/kg in May to 32,943 won/kg for Jun 1-11, 2026.
Mulberries ripen in early to mid June and finish by mid to late June.
A black raspberry picked about four times between early June and early July. A 2016 newspaper report said prices had collapsed that year.
Sources split between Jun-Jul and Jul-Sep. The early Northland type matures in early June, and greenhouse fruit appears from March.
caveat: One wiki's list says Jul-Sep, while a travel guide says Jun-Jul.

blurb: Korean-grown cherries ripen from late May to mid June. Gyeongju is the largest region, with 70 ha and about 10% of national output.
A small fruit with a short shelf life, so little reaches shops. People make jam, syrup, liqueur and tea. Don't chew the seed.
The fruit of ornamental cherry trees on streets and hillsides. It is foraged rather than sold. Hobbyists steep it in soju, at about 1 part fruit to 1 part sugar to 2 parts soju, for 3-4 months.
Encyclopedias give no month for apricots. The Jun-Jul window comes only from a government fruit database.
caveat: Only that one database gives the window.

blurb: A fruit grown in Wando greenhouses since 2010, about 130 t a year in 2022. Namhae and Geoje grow it outdoors. No source gives a Korean harvest month.
eat: Peeled and eaten around the large seed
caveat: Sources disagree. One wiki implies summer, while Korean Wikipedia says late winter to early spring.

blurb: Green plums are picked from late May to mid June, and people buy them Jun 5-20 to make maesil syrup. Yellow hwangmae comes after the mangjong solar term. Korea's food safety ministry says ripe hwangmae cuts cyanide compounds by about 70%.
A peach with nectarine-like skin that opens the peach season. It sells out in about 10 days, which shoppers call bokketing, a mash-up of boksunga (peach) and ticketing.

Peaches arrive in a relay of cultivars, each lasting about 15 days. Changbangjosaeng comes in mid Jul, mibaekdo in late Jul, cheonjungdo in mid Aug and janghowon-hwangdo in early to mid Sep. Ttakbok is firm and mulbok is soft.
Plums run from mid July to early August. Gimcheon leads, with daeseok first and humusa after.
A melon from Seongju, which supplies roughly 80-85% of the national crop. Greenhouse fruit starts early, and the first Seongju fruit of 2026 shipped on Jan 19.
festivals: Seongju Chamoe & Life Culture Festival, May 14-17, 2026

blurb: Watermelon in season from June to August, with August the tail. Gochang held its official shipping ceremony on Jun 5, 2025, for fruit of 7-9 kg and 13 Brix or more.
Sold all year, with the best months Jul-Sep. Gokseong fruit starts from mid May.

A tomato from salty, brackish soil in Gangseo, Busan, and it tastes a little salty. The official name is Daejeo tomato, but outside Daejeo-dong it is called jjapjjari. The harvest starts in Feb and peaks in March.
Greenhouses grow cherry tomatoes all year, so no month marks the season. The government farm portal lists it in March, and one wiki calls it a summer fruit.
A domestic mango led by Jeju that ships mostly Jun-Jul. In 2023, early Gangjin fruit sold above 300,000 won per 3 kg, against a June average near 100,000 won.
An early apple that is replacing aori as the first of the year. It is ready in mid to late July.
An early apple sold in August. Korea's farm agency puts it in late August, and Summer King is replacing it.
caveat: Sources say Aug, and late Aug from the farm agency.

blurb: The Chuseok apple, named for the autumn harvest holiday. It ripens in September, around the holiday. In 2026 the crop ripened early, according to a news agency.
A late-season apple that ripens in early to mid October. A news site puts it in early Oct. It sits between hongro and buse in the ripening order.
A late-season apple that Korea's farm agency places in early to mid October. It ripens alongside Shinano Gold.
The last apple in the ripening order. Only one low-authority guide gives a month, Oct-Nov, and it names Cheongsong.
An early pear that ships mainly in August, ahead of singo at Chuseok, the autumn harvest holiday.
The standard Korean pear, in season Sep-Nov. In 2026 full supply began in the second week of September, when daily volume rose from 17.8 t to 137.5 t. Naju is the named region.
A Campbell Early grape. The only month source is a low-authority guide that gives Aug-Oct, so treat that as a lead.
A Kyoho grape, sourced to a single wiki page. It runs late Aug to mid Sep.
Sold Sep-Dec, though that window is weakly sourced. Retail price was 16,572 won per 2 kg on Sep 2, 2026, 41.1% below Sep 2023. Sangju and Gimcheon are the named regions.
Figs ship from mid July to October, with August as the peak. Yeongam is the main region. Jeonnam province grew from 673 ha and 6,570 t in 2020 to 741 ha and 11,530 t in 2025.
A crisp persimmon eaten while firm. Buyu, the main cultivar, ripens late Oct to early Nov and keeps 4-5 months in cold storage. The early seochonjosaeng from late Sep is a weak type.
caveat: A rural economics institute forecast 2026 output down 14.1% after heat and drought.

blurb: A large astringent persimmon bred for hongsi, the soft ripe kind. Hadong Akyang and Yeongam both hold protected geographical indications. No source names its months.
caveat: The late Oct window is inferred from other large astringent types.

blurb: A seedless astringent persimmon unique to Cheongdo. It ripens in late October, and a festival runs each October.
Picked from late Oct to late Nov and then left to ripen further. Chamdarae is the name given to Korean kiwifruit. Haenam gold kiwi is picked late Oct to early Nov.
Chinese quince, which reaches markets from early October. The guide behind that date is about making quince liqueur.
caveat: The months rest on a blog and a 1993 article.

blurb: A red berry picked in mid to late September. People make cheong syrup in Sep-Oct. Mungyeong is the best-known source.
A small wild kiwi that ripens in Sep-Oct. Cultivated fruit comes late Aug to early Oct.
A wild grape that blackens in September, with seeds ripe in Sep-Oct.
Cornelian cherry from Gurye, where the harvest was in full swing in mid November in 2020.
The Sep-Dec window is a season of sale, not a harvest date. Sour types are sold as juice or concentrate, and sweet types are mostly imported. Goheung holds the geographical indication.
Chestnuts ripen from late August for the earliest types, and late types after late September. Buyers usually start about Sep 1. One wiki says the months after harvest suit eating best.
No source gives its months, so October is an estimate from festival timing in Boeun and Gyeongsan. Boeun's fresh output in 2025 was forecast at about 1,982 t, up 27%.
Walnuts are picked from mid September to early October, depending on cultivar. Cheonan Gwangdeok is the historic name.
Pine nuts come from cones picked in Sep-Oct. Gapyeong output fell from 2,205 t in 2014 to 24 t in 2023. A kilo of cones yields only about 50-60 g of shelled nuts.
eat: On 식혜 or 수정과, sweet drinks

blurb: The nuts are gathered when the fruit falls, Oct-Nov. Limit how many you eat. One wiki says adults should stay under about 20 a day, and Korean Wikipedia warns children against 5 or more a day.
Harvested mid to late October, sourced to two wiki pages. Udo island off Jeju is the named origin. In Gyeongsang province people eat them boiled in salt water.
Imported all year. Domestic growing is trial scale, in Jeju greenhouses and a few other places, so it has no season.
Mostly imported from the Philippines and Thailand, so it has no season. The first domestic harvest was in 1964, and imports took over from the 1980s.
No source gives a season for passion fruit, so it stays off the calendar.
No source gives a season for plumcot, so it stays off the calendar.
